title: A noise from a hidden toy helped more ten-month-olds find it than younger infants
summary: Moore and Meltzoff found that sound from a hidden object raised search success at 10 months much more than at 8.75 months.
body: In the second experiment of that 2008 paper, the hidden object was either sounding or silent. With sound, 21 of 32 infants at 10 months succeeded, against 5 of 32 infants at 8.75 months. The authors report that sound clues significantly increased success on total hiding for the older group, and not for the younger group. The counts are that sample. They are not a rate for all children.

sources.title: Factors affecting infants' manual search for occluded objects and the genesis of object permanence
sources.author: M. Keith Moore and Andrew N. Meltzoff
sources.note: Supports Experiment 2: sound increased total-occlusion success at 10 months (21 of 32) and not at 8.75 months (5 of 32).
